text.p: Ameritech Corp. said Tuesday it had notified federal regulators it was withdrawing its application to provide long-distance phone service in Michigan, ending its bid to become the first Baby Bell to offer such service in its local-calling area.
The decision came after the Federal Communications Commission said Friday it would not consider key evidence submitted by Ameritech as part of the application.

Under the new telecommunications act, Ameritech and the other regional Baby Bells must prove to regulators that they have opened their local phone monopolies to new competitors before gaining access to the long-distance market.
The FCC noted Friday that Michigan regulators said they had not yet approved Ameritech's "interconnection" agreement with AT&T Corp. at the time it made its most recent filing.
In a statement Tuesday, Ameritech said it anticipated that the status of the approval of its contract with AT&T in Michigan will be resolved.
